messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER: High packet loss detected at CDN POP eu-west-1 (15% packet loss, 06:12 UTC). Affected routes: edge-eu-west-1.*. Paging oncall-sre Priya.
Priya: acked, looking. seeing spikes across multiple probes, p95 latency +300ms, error budget alert firing. starting graphed metrics.
Priya: run mtr to edge POP from kibana-probe:
```
MTR to edge-eu-west-1.pop.redwood.net (52.31.12.7), 10 cycles:
  1. 10.0.1.1        0.0%   1ms
  2. 198.51.100.1    0.0%  12ms
  3. 203.0.113.45   15.0%  85ms  (loss at transit)
  4. edge-eu-west-1 15.0%  90ms
```
Priya: loss looks like last-mile / upstream peering blips at hop 3. opening ticket with CDN provider. @NetEng can you validate BGP churn?
NetEng: pulling BGP updates now — I see a burst of withdrawn prefixes 06:10–06:14 UTC on the primary transit, AS64532. Path prepends + communities changed by provider.
Marco: provider-side peering issue would explain packet loss across multiple customers. Can we reduce traffic to that POP and shift to eu-central-1 / eu-north?
Priya: yes, plan: set pop weight eu-west-1 -> 30%, eu-central-1 -> 70% for edge routing; lower DNS LB weight and shift streaming session affinity. Also reduce DNS TTL to 30s for apex and streaming subdomains.
Claire: are customers actively affected? SupportBot, any alerts?
SupportBot: two customer support tickets flagged degraded streaming in EU at 06:15. Error types: 502 for API fetches, streaming disconnects. Estimated impacted requests: ~0.9% of EU requests in the window. Top impacted customers: acme-corp, marketlytics.
Dan: putting a short status note to status.redwood.com? we should avoid panic, mark "Degraded performance - partial" for EU region.
Priya: I'll create incident timeline and send to status. Taking immediate mitigation:
- Adjusting traffic weights in traffic-controller: `trafficctl set-pop-weight --pop eu-west-1 --weight 30`
- `trafficctl set-pop-weight --pop eu-central-1 --weight 70`
- Lowering DNS TTL: `gcloud dns record-sets transaction start && ... --ttl=30`
Marco: prepping BGP community change to prefer alternate transit, will ask provider to apply NO_EXPORT for problematic peer. Sending provider slack thread now.
NetEng: provider acknowledged intermittent peering flap, they are inserting a filter to stop route flapping. ETA for full fix ~20–30m.
Evan: taking over on-call for remediation (handoff). Priya — update handoff notes and add mitigation steps to the incident doc.
Priya: handoff notes added. Current state: traffic shifted, DNS TTL lowered, provider applying filters. Packet loss dropped from 15% -> 1.2% in the last 5m. continuing to monitor.
Claire: can we proactively notify the two impacted customers? Suggest short recap + ETA. Dan, want to own customer comms?
Dan: happy to. Draft: "We observed CDN edge connectivity issues in EU (eu-west-1) causing streaming reconnects and elevated error rates between 06:10–06:30 UTC. Workaround applied by shifting traffic to eu-central-1; provider is applying peering fixes. We'll follow up with post-incident report"
SupportBot: sent customer outreach to acme-corp and marketlytics with the above draft.
Priya: monitoring graphs: now p95 latency back to baseline, loss ~0.4%. Some residual errors on long-lived streams that were tied to earlier client disconnects. Queued retries are clearing.
Marco: provider confirmed they added a mitigation to stop flap and re-advertised stable routes. Asking them for root cause (fiber congestion on partner handoff) and timeline for permanent remediation.
Evan: status update to channel — MITIGATED (partial): traffic rerouted, provider filter applied. Monitoring for 1h, then will revert pop weight slowly.
Priya: leaving notes for postmortem: timeline, graphs, commands run, customer impact summary, and a suggestion to add automatic POP-weight failover when packet loss >5% for 3m.
Dan: adding incident to postmortem board and assigning to Priya + Marco.
Claire: thumbs up. Anything else?
NetEng: recommend adding synthetic checks from multiple last-mile probes across key ISPs in EU so we detect peering regressions faster.
Priya: agreed. I'll file an action item. Closing slack thread to reduce noise, will append final summary once provider root cause is confirmed. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity set to S2 - regional degradation. Duration: 06:10–06:28 UTC. Current status: monitoring.
